registered: 2026-09-30, before any GPU run (DECISION.md, Backend parity tiers)

revisions.note: the numbers below, with the v1 rules: strict public numbers compared raw at 1e-4 (score unscaled, a server answer unrounded), q8_0 row = the q8_0 derivation, server_no_act_head allowed in both tiers, a missing public answer only counted; every gate JSON written before v2 used them

revisions.before: the v2 re-gate of the saved runs and the step-8 runs (build-4b/parity/v2)
changes: strict-f32 public numbers: a candidate number whose reference number is 4-digit (the reference rounds its answers, a server answer is not rounded) is rounded with Python round(x, 4) first; a score error is divided by K - 1 (its range), as the derivation and the f16-class report always did; public_atol stays 1e-4 (both sides 4-digit: the error is a whole number of 1e-4 steps, the boundary rule passes one step)
server_no_act_head: dropped from strict-f32; in f16-class it passes only for a whole run without act logits (a server build before debug.act_logits), never for some questions of a run that has them
a missing public answer fails (v1 only counted it)

f16-class q8_0 row = the f16 row: no device quantizes activations (CUDA dequantizes Q8_0 since step 6), so a Q8_0 device run is gated against a CPU baseline with F32 activations by the f16 numbers; the v1 q8_0 numbers move to activation_quantized and apply only to a candidate that quantizes activations, against a baseline that quantizes them the same way
the baseline activation class is enforced from the identity records (check_identity)
max_abs_dp is a sanity bound for gross errors (it does not discriminate between backends; the mean bound and the flip rule carry f16-class)

derivation: python3 tests/laya/parity/derive_tiers.py --p4 <Phase 4 parity outputs> --check tests/laya/parity/tiers.json; each number = 2 x the largest value seen in the CPU pairs of its class, rounded up to one significant digit

strict-f32.baseline: PyTorch fp32 reference on the CPU (verify_reference.py ref), same checkpoint revision as the GGUF

f16-class.baseline: CPU run of the same GGUF whose activations are F32: kernels blas (or auto resolving to cpu+blas), or any CPU kernels on an F32 GGUF. A candidate that quantizes activations (identity runtime.activations, or CPU default / repack kernels on a quantized GGUF) needs a baseline that quantizes them the same way and the activation_quantized numbers
f16-class.argmax: a flip passes only when the baseline top-2 probability gap (softmax of the raw scorer logits, T = 1) is below flip_max_gap
